dedupe_keys.name: bilsdale transmitter fire and the restoration of tv and radio in north east england 2021 to 2022

description: This post-event and recovery case covers the loss of the Bilsdale transmitting station in North Yorkshire after a fire on 10 August 2021, and the regulator's review of how services were restored. Bilsdale, owned and run by Arqiva, carried free-to-air television and radio to up to 670,000 homes from York to Middlesbrough; the mast was so badly damaged that it had to be demolished. Arqiva brought in temporary transmitters, and a temporary 80-metre mast at the site began operating on 13 October 2021. Ofcom's incident review, published in June 2022, found delays in bringing the temporary transmitters into service, especially at Bilsdale itself, caused by site access, planning and technical problems, some linked to the site lying in a National Park and a Site of Special Scientific Interest; it also found that information to viewers and listeners was at first too general and targeted help for households came late. Ofcom asked the organisations that deliver broadcasting to review their recovery plans and their support for affected audiences, and said it could act further if needed. Coverage: one main transmitter and its relay network, August 2021 to 2022. Format and access: review statement as a PDF and news release on the Ofcom website, free. Caveats: the cause of the fire is not given in the sources read; Ofcom's site refused automated access, so figures come from Ofcom's news page as quoted in search results and trade press. Simulation uses: single-point-of-failure analysis of broadcast networks, restoration time modelling and emergency communication planning. Related records: the Ofcom broadcast transmitter parameters dataset lists the affected transmitters.
